solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poignancy, though in former times, mostly

indicators.note: 'in' places one piece within another, so the short though sits within the shortened past
'mostly' means not quite all, so PAST keeps all but its final letter

parts.note: PAST (former times) without its last letter
tho is the informal spelling of though

explanation.surface: Someone reflecting that a certain sadness belonged mostly to the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: Though looks like a link word tying the halves together; it is a piece of the wordplay in its informal spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: pathos is the quality in a story or scene that stirs pity, which is what poignancy names.

clue.text: Write note in a single sheet attachment

indicators.note: 'in' places the written note within the sheet, as words go on a page

parts.note: the article taken as it stands
a page is a single sheet of a book
to pen is to write
D is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: An instruction to jot a note on a single sheet sent as an attachment, like an email file.
explanation.walkthrough: Attachment makes you think of a file sent with an email; the definition is an add-on or limb, and the single sheet is a book's.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an appendage is anything attached to something larger, from a limb to a supplement.

clue.text: Captive deer trapped in weed

indicators.note: something trapped in a thing is enclosed by it, so the deer goes inside the weeding word

parts.note: to hoe is to weed a bed
a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: A deer caught fast in a tangle of weeds, held captive.
explanation.walkthrough: Weed looks like a noun, a plant for the deer to be tangled in; it is the gardening verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Captive as a noun: a hostage is a person held by force to secure a bargain.

clue.text: What's leading summer each year? Spring

indicators.note: what leads a word is its front, so take the first letter of summer

parts.note: the first letter of summer
p.a., per annum, is Latin for each year

explanation.surface: A riddle about the seasons: what comes before summer every year? Spring, of course.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants spring to be the season that leads summer; it is a mineral spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring in its sense of a natural source of water: a spa is a mineral spring, and by extension the resort around it.

clue.text: Count rat in a way to be this?

definitions.text: Count rat in a way to be this?

indicators.note: putting letters in another way means rearranging them

parts.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: A count who rats on his side is asked whether that makes him one.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a count who ratted, changing sides, would be exactly this.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat is to betray your side, and one who does so is a turncoat, so the whole clue reads straight.

clue.text: Character in Iliad who volunteered to serve

wordplay.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve, with its article

explanation.surface: A figure from Homer's Iliad who stepped forward to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iliad makes you think of a hero such as Achilles; the character is a letter of the Greek alphabet. The TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time volunteer army, so those who volunteered are THE TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Character in its sense of a written letter: theta is a letter of the Greek alphabet the Iliad is written in.

clue.text: Answer lies in handy loom needing no fittings

parts.note: handy, ready to hand

indicators.note: something that lies in a place rests inside it, so the answer's A sits within the looming word

parts.note: to loom over is to tower
A is the standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A craft tip: the solution lies in a handy loom that needs no extra fittings.
explanation.walkthrough: Loom looks like the weaving frame, which suits the clothing answer; it is the verb, to loom or tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: ready-to-wear clothes come in standard sizes, so no tailor's fittings are required.

clue.text: Blimp perhaps endlessly circling good German city

indicators.note: without an end, so the last letter of COLONEL is dropped
to circle something is to go round it, so the shortened colonel surrounds the letter for good

parts.note: COLONEL, as in Colonel Blimp, without its last letter
G is the usual abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: An airship endlessly circling above a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: Blimp suggests an airship; it is Colonel Blimp, a pompous old British officer from a 1930s newspaper cartoon, so Blimp is an example of a colonel.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain naming: Cologne (Köln) is a city on the Rhine in western Germany.

clue.text: This is noble, the third exiled from ancient Spanish kingdom

indicators.note: to be exiled is to be sent out, so the third letter is removed

parts.note: Aragon was a medieval kingdom in north-east Spain
the kingdom loses its third letter, A

explanation.surface: A nobleman forced into exile from an old Spanish kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: Noble suggests a Spanish grandee; here it is chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: argon is one of the noble gases, so 'this is noble' is a chemist's way of pointing to it.

clue.text: Renegade with an attitude about tattoo

parts.note: an is the article A

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the attitude is wrapped around the tattoo

parts.note: a pose is an attitude struck
tat is short for tattoo

explanation.surface: A rebel with attitude, and a tattoo to prove it.
explanation.walkthrough: The tattoo and the attitude paint a rebel, which fits the definition, but the definition is the religious sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an apostate abandons their faith or party, as a renegade does.

clue.text: Claim everything for instance European

parts.note: all = everything
e.g., for instance
E for European

explanation.surface: Someone claiming everything, a European for example.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces simply run in the order the clue gives them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to allege is to claim something, usually without proof.

clue.text: Is any train running in an unclean state?

indicators.note: letters that are running are on the move, not staying in their printed order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A passenger asking if any train is running in a filthy condition.
explanation.walkthrough: Running looks like a train in service; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: insanitary describes a place dirty enough to be a health risk.

clue.text: Cheeky rascal reconfigured internet

indicators.note: to reconfigure is to set up in a new arrangement, so the letters of internet are reordered

parts.note: an imp is a little rascal
anagram of INTERNET

explanation.surface: A cheeky young rascal who has reconfigured the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheeky and rascal sit side by side like a single description; the rascal belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: impertinent describes a lack of respect, the same cheek a rascal shows.

clue.text: Essential part of analysing unknown sticky substance

indicators.note: the essential part of something is its core, so the answer sits inside the following words

parts.note: found across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A lab testing an unknown sticky substance.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words, from the last letter of analysing into unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word: gunk is any sticky, messy substance.

clue.text: Weak eddying causing water turbulence

indicators.note: eddying water swirls round, so the letters swirl into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 4 letters

explanation.surface: Feeble eddies stirring up the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Eddying fits the watery surface so well it barely looks like an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a wake is the churned water left behind a moving boat.

clue.text: Wonderful friend guarding female round soldiers

indicators.note: a guard stands around what it protects, so the friend surrounds the middle pieces

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a hen is a female bird
O is round in shape
soldiers are men, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A marvellous friend who protects a woman surrounded by soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Round reads as surrounding, a second container signal; it is only the letter O, run on in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: phenomenal describes something extraordinary enough to wonder at.

clue.text: Go out — be coming back holding key?

indicators.note: something coming back travels the opposite way, so be is reversed
to hold is to contain, so the reversed word has the key inside it

parts.note: the word taken as it stands
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: Leave, and then come back with the key.
explanation.walkthrough: Go out is the tide going out; the surface makes it a person leaving the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The tidal sense: water that recedes from the shore is said to ebb.

clue.text: Muscles suffering, reportedly letting oneself down

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the answer only sounds like the wordplay

parts.note: abs are stomach muscles; ailing is suffering

explanation.surface: Aching muscles letting someone down.
explanation.walkthrough: Letting oneself down reads as failing; it is lowering yourself on a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal reading of an idiom: abseiling is descending a cliff by rope, lowering your own body.

clue.text: With some chance of restoration theatre being OK to broadcast

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
fit to air, to put on radio or TV

explanation.surface: A Restoration theatre play just about fit to be broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Restoration theatre suggests the English drama after 1660; the definition takes restoration as plain mending.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: whatever can be mended stands some chance of being restored.

clue.text: Quite a hit introducing new museum piece

indicators.note: something hit is knocked about, so quite and a are jumbled
to introduce is to bring in, so the letter for new is placed inside the jumble

parts.note: anagram of QUITE A
N is short for new

explanation.surface: A new exhibit that has proved quite a hit with museum-goers.
explanation.walkthrough: Hit reads as a success; it is the anagram signal, striking the letters apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an antique is an old object of the kind museums display.

clue.text: Son in company of soldiers is intimate and relaxed

indicators.note: 'in' places one piece within another, so the son sits inside the company

parts.note: Coy is the military abbreviation for a company
S for son

explanation.surface: A son serving with his company feels at ease.
explanation.walkthrough: Company alone would give CO; the full phrase company of soldiers points to the army's own abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: cosy describes somewhere warm, snug and informal.

clue.text: Starch fool's put in sparkling wine

indicators.note: to put something in is to insert it, so the fool goes inside the wine

parts.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An odd recipe where starch and a fool go into fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: Fool looks like the fruit pudding, which fits a recipe; it is a silly person. The ’s stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: cassava is a tropical root grown for its starch, the source of tapioca.

clue.text: Let It Be and Time included in sequence of songs

indicators.note: to be included in is to be taken inside, so time goes inside the set

parts.note: a band's set is its sequence of songs
T for time

explanation.surface: A band's setlist featuring the Beatles' Let It Be and a song called Time.
explanation.walkthrough: Let It Be is dressed as the Beatles song; it is a proofreader's instruction, Latin for let it stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A proofreading term: stet, written in a margin, tells the printer to let a deleted word be.

clue.text: Author with a popular following beginning to tire

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so with, a and popular come after the first letter of tire
the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of tire
W is short for with
the article as it stands
in = popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A popular writer whose readers are starting to lose interest.
explanation.walkthrough: A popular following looks like a writer's fan base; following is the order instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Mark Twain wrote Huckleberry Finn.

clue.text: Trainee's job in winter stripped navy vessel

indicators.note: a stripped word has its outer layer removed, so winter loses both end letters

parts.note: WINTER without its first and last letters
RN, the Royal Navy
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: A trainee sailor's winter job aboard a stripped-down naval vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Navy and vessel make a naval picture, but the answer is office work experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an internship is the post an intern, a trainee, holds.

clue.text: Teacher's to show disapproval over unclothed form

indicators.note: unclothed means bare, stripped of its outer layer, so form loses its end letters
in a down clue, over means above, so the tut is placed on top

parts.note: to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval
FORM without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A teacher tutting at a nude figure in life drawing class.
explanation.walkthrough: Form suggests the human body; it only supplies letters. The ’s stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tutor is a teacher, especially one who teaches individuals or small groups.

clue.text: Brand horse queen's breaking in

indicators.note: to break in is to force entry, so the queen gets inside the horse

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
QU is a standard abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: Branding a horse while the queen is breaking it in.
explanation.walkthrough: Brand and breaking in paint a ranch; brand is the product name, and breaking in is the insertion signal. The ’s stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the car world: a marque is a manufacturer's make, its brand name.

clue.text: Mistake in recording tailless reptile

indicators.note: without a tail, so the last letter of TAPING goes
'in' places one piece within another, so the mistake sits inside the shortened recording

parts.note: TAPING (recording) without its last letter
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A slip-up while recording a reptile that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Tailless seems to describe the reptile, as lizards shed tails; it acts on the recording.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, one kind of reptile.

clue.text: Capital not all needed for equipment

indicators.note: not all of the word is used, so the final letter is left off

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
the city without its last letter

explanation.surface: Not all of the money needed to buy equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital reads as money; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a rig is a set of equipment, as in a drilling rig or a sound rig.

clue.text: Developer of fashionable IOW resort, name forgotten

indicators.note: what is forgotten is left out, so the N for name drops from the resort

parts.note: in = fashionable
VENTNOR, a resort on the Isle of Wight (IOW, off England's south coast), without one N for name

explanation.surface: A property developer who built a smart Isle of Wight resort, now forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: Developer suggests property; it means someone who develops new things.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an inventor develops new devices and processes.

clue.text: Called to enter grand English country house

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the calling word goes between grand and English

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
rang = called on the phone
E for English

explanation.surface: Invited to visit a grand English country house.
explanation.walkthrough: Grand looks like an adjective for the house; it is a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a grange is a country house, originally one with farm buildings attached.
